adults.title: Taking Down the Sign on the Gate
adults.big_idea: We do not have to perfect ourselves before we come to Jesus Christ; we come to Him as we are, with a willing heart, and He perfects us.
adults.objective: Learners will name one thing that makes them feel unworthy to come to the Savior, choose one way to come to Him anyway this week, and choose one person to invite.
prepare: Read Elder Dube’s talk, “Come unto Christ,” and mark the three truths he draws from Moroni 10:32.
Write on a sheet of paper: Trespassers will be prosecuted. Tape it to the board or the door before class.
Write on the board, covered or folded back until needed: Come. Deny yourselves. Be perfected in Him.
Bring a slip of paper and a pencil for each person.
Pray by name for the people you will teach, especially any who may feel they do not measure up.

segments.name: The sign on the gate
steps: After the prayer, point to the sign and ask the first question. Take two or three short answers.

Tell the story in your own words: in 1987 Elder Dube was a young missionary who had been a member of the Church for only two years. That sign hung on the gate of the mission office. President Oaks asked that it be removed to avoid any impression of exclusion, because we invite all to come unto Christ.

Say that Elder Dube gained in that moment the desire to love others as the Savior does. Then ask the second question and let it sit in silence for a few seconds before moving on. No one needs to answer aloud.
questions: If you saw this sign on a gate, what would it tell you about the people inside?
Is there any part of your life where you have felt a sign like this between you and the Savior?

segments.name: Three truths in one verse
steps: Uncover the three phrases on the board. Invite everyone to open to Moroni 10:32 and have one person read it aloud.

Divide the room into three groups (or three rows). Give each group one phrase and read them what Elder Dube said about it from the key quotes: Come is an action; Deny yourselves means surrender and letting go; Be perfected in Him means coming as we are with a willing heart.
Give the groups three minutes to talk about their question below, then ask one person from each group to report in a sentence or two.

Read together Elder Dube’s summary: “We do not need to perfect ourselves to come to Christ. We come to Christ to be perfected.” Ask a learner to restate it in his or her own words as a quick check for understanding.
Read President Nelson’s words, which Elder Dube quoted, from the aligned quotes. Ask how the phrase about perfection being pending changes the way we feel about our present weaknesses.
questions: Come: What does moving toward the Savior actually look like on an ordinary Tuesday?
Deny yourselves: Why does letting go feel like losing something, when Elder Dube calls it surrender?
Be perfected in Him: What is the difference between a perfect heart and a willing heart?

segments.name: One more ministering visit
steps: Retell the story faithfully: on the way to the airport, a stake president asked Elder Dube to make one more ministering visit, to Brother Randall Child, a good man trying very hard to stop smoking. Elder Dube prayed that Heavenly Father would put words in his mouth. He asked Brother Child how much he loved his wife, Laurin, and then invited the two of them to find a quiet room and choose a date to be sealed in the house of the Lord. They came back with a date, and two months later they were sealed.
Ask a good reader to read what Sister Child later shared (the key quote from T23.21).
In pairs, have learners discuss the first two questions for three minutes.

Invite one or two pairs to share. Then read Elder Dube’s conclusion that Brother Child came to Christ with prayer, with trust and with a willing heart, and that the Savior through His grace helped him let go of what was holding him back.
questions: Sister Child watched her husband suffer from wanting to be perfect in every way. Where do you see that same suffering among people you love, or in yourself?
How is doing the very best we can different from giving up on change?
Notice that the invitation was to choose a date, not to be finished first. What does that teach about how the Lord works with us?

segments.name: The sign on the gate of the heart
steps: Explain that Elder Dube said the adversary wants to hang the sign on the gate of our heart. He named addiction, doubt, pride, pain, grief, guilt and materialism, or whatever is holding us back, and said the adversary tells us this makes us unworthy to come unto Christ.

Hand out the slips of paper. Invite learners to write privately, for two minutes, one thing that has made them feel they must stay away, and beneath it one way they could come to the Savior this week as they are. Assure them no one will collect or read the slips.
While they write, read Moroni 10:33 aloud slowly, and then President Oaks’s words from the aligned quotes: “His grace is for all.”
Take down the paper sign from the board or door and set it aside without comment.
questions: What would it look like to take that sign down this week?

segments.name: Find one person
steps: Read Elder Dube’s invitation to us all (T23.28) and the promise he attached to it: as we lose ourselves in helping someone come unto Christ, we will find solutions to our current problems. Have someone read Matthew 16:25.

Mention that he also spoke to a former missionary whose testimony is not as certain as it once was, and to all who feel that same ache, inviting them to come unto Christ and embrace His promise of joy (John 15:11).
Ask learners to turn their slip over and write one name the Spirit brings to mind, and one simple step: a text, a visit, a seat saved, an invitation to meet with the missionaries.
Invite one or two to share how they have seen their own burdens lighten while helping someone else.
questions: Who is one person you could invite, and what is the smallest honest first step?

segments.name: Witness and follow-up
steps: Bear a brief testimony that the Savior’s invitation has no sign on the gate, using Elder Dube’s witness that He suffered for us in Gethsemane and on the cross because He is completely devoted to all of us.

Tell the class that next week you will begin by asking two questions: What happened when you came to Him as you were? What happened when you invited your one person? Ask them to keep the slip in their scriptures or phone case as a reminder.
Close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: We do not need to perfect ourselves to come to Christ. We come to Christ to be perfected.
Be perfected in Him: Come as we are with a willing heart. He will give us a new heart.
In the early hours of the morning, the answer came very clear: ‘Randall doesn’t need to be perfect. He needs to do the very best he can.’
The adversary wants to hang that sign on the gate of our heart.

scriptures.use: Read verse 32 aloud, then study its three phrases in three groups. Read verse 33 slowly while learners write in silence.
Optional cross-reference for the third group: read it and ask who does the work of giving the new heart.
Read with Elder Dube’s invitation to find one person; ask what we find when we lose ourselves for the Savior’s sake.
Read as the promise offered to anyone whose testimony feels less certain than it once was.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Russell M. Nelson
aligned_quotes.text: Perfection is pending. It can come in full only after the Resurrection and only through the Lord. It awaits all who love Him and keep His commandments.

invitations.text: I invite you, please come unto Christ and embrace His promise
My humble invitation to us all: Will you find one person and invite him or her to come unto Christ by exercising faith to follow His teachings, or invite a friend to meet with the missionaries?

takeaways: I do not have to be perfect to come to Christ; I come to Christ to be perfected.
The Lord asks for a willing heart and my very best, and His grace helps me let go of what holds me back.
As I help one person come unto Christ, I will find solutions to my own problems.
act: Each day this week, come to the Savior as you are in one concrete way: an honest prayer, the sacrament, a visit with the bishop, a temple appointment on the calendar.
Choose one thing that is holding you back and take one step to let go of it, asking for the Savior’s help by name in prayer.
Reach out to the one person whose name you wrote, and invite him or her to something specific: church, a family meal and scripture, or a visit with the missionaries.
Tell someone who is struggling that he or she does not need to be perfect to come.
adapt: At home or with only two or three people: skip the groups and talk through the three phrases together, one question each.
Large class: keep the three-phrase study in rows and use pairs for everything else so everyone speaks at least once.
Only 15 minutes: do the sign story, read Moroni 10:32 with the three truths, read Sister Child’s answer to prayer, and end with the two written lines on the slip.

youth.title: Come As You Are
youth.big_idea: Jesus Christ invites us to come to Him as we are; we do not fix ourselves first, because He is the one who perfects us.
youth.objective: Youth will explain in their own words why they do not need to be perfect to come to Christ, and will choose one way to come to Him and one person to invite this week.
prepare: Read Elder Dube’s talk, “Come unto Christ.”
Write Trespassers will be prosecuted on a sheet of paper and tape it to the classroom door at eye level before anyone arrives.
Bring paper, pens or markers, and tape. Youth will need their scriptures or phones.
Write three headings on the board: Come. Deny yourselves. Be perfected in Him.

segments.name: What does the sign say about us?
steps: As youth come in, say nothing about the sign on the door. After the prayer, hand each pair a sheet of paper and give them 60 seconds to list as many keep-out messages as they can think of from daily life: signs, locked accounts, group chats they are not in, tables where there is no seat.
Have the pair with the longest list read theirs. Then ask the question.
questions: How does it feel to be on the wrong side of a keep-out sign?

segments.name: The sign comes down
steps: Tell the story: in 1987 Elder Dube was a young missionary, only two years a member of the Church. The sign on the gate of the mission office said exactly what is taped to our door. President Oaks asked that it be removed to avoid any impression of exclusion, because we invite all to come unto Christ.
Ask a youth to go and take the sign off the door and bring it to the front. Keep it; you will use it again.

Read President Oaks’s words from the aligned quotes about why the Savior suffered for us. If you wish, have someone read Luke 22:44 and ask what it shows about how devoted He is to each person in the room.
questions: Why do you think one sign mattered so much to President Oaks?

segments.name: Three teams, three truths
steps: Have everyone find Moroni 10:32 and read it aloud together.

Form three teams and give each one heading from the board. Read each team what Elder Dube said about its phrase (key quotes T23.07 to T23.09, including T23.08: surrender, and let go of the things that are holding us back).
Give teams three minutes to make a poster for their phrase: a six-word summary and a quick sketch that would make sense to a friend who has never read the Book of Mormon.
Each team presents in 30 seconds. Let the class vote by applause for the clearest poster. Tape all three to the wall.
Read Elder Dube’s one-line summary (T23.10) and ask two youth to say it back in their own words.
questions: Which of the three is hardest for people your age: moving, letting go, or believing He can change you?

segments.name: Do I have to fix myself first?
steps: Tell the story of the ministering visit: Elder Dube, on his way to the airport, was asked to visit Brother Randall Child, a good man trying very hard to stop smoking. Elder Dube had no idea what to say and prayed for words. He asked Brother Child how much he loved his wife, Laurin, and invited them to choose a date to be sealed in the house of the Lord. They chose one, and two months later they were sealed.
Have a youth read Sister Child’s answer to prayer (key quote T23.21).
In pairs, discuss the first two questions for three minutes. Then take a few answers from the whole group.

Be honest that Elder Dube also spoke of a former missionary who wrote that his testimony is not as certain as it once was. Elder Dube did not scold him. He invited him, and all who feel that same ache, to come unto Christ and embrace His promise of joy. Read John 15:11 together.
Share Elder Rasband’s line from the aligned quotes and ask the last question.
questions: Why do we sometimes think we have to clean ourselves up before we pray, come to church or talk to the bishop?
What is the difference between doing your very best and pretending to be perfect?
If a friend told you his or her testimony was not as sure as it used to be, what would you say after hearing this talk?

segments.name: Take your own sign down
steps: Hold up the sign from the door. Explain that Elder Dube said the adversary wants to hang it on the gate of our heart, telling us that doubt, pride, pain, guilt, addiction or whatever is holding us back makes us unworthy to come unto Christ.
Give each youth a small piece of paper. In silence, for two minutes, they write one thing that makes them feel they should stay away from the Savior. No names, and no one will read it.
Invite them to fold it and write on the outside one way they will come to Him this week anyway. They keep the paper.
Tear the door sign in half and put it in the bin.

segments.name: The one-person challenge
steps: Read Elder Dube’s invitation to us all (T23.28) and his promise: as you lose yourself in helping someone come unto Christ, you will find solutions to your current problems. Have someone read Matthew 16:25.

Ask each youth to think of one person and one real invitation they could give by next Sunday: come to a youth activity, sit with me at church, come to seminary, meet the missionaries at our house. They may type a draft message on their phone now but do not need to send it in class.
Invite two or three to share their plan, without naming the person if that would embarrass anyone.
Tell them you will ask next week: Whom did you invite, and what happened to your own week when you did? Bear a short testimony that the Savior wants them as they are, and close with prayer.
questions: What usually stops us from inviting, and what would make it easier?

key_quotes.text: We do not need to perfect ourselves to come to Christ. We come to Christ to be perfected.
Come: It’s an action. We choose to move from our current place to a better place.
Be perfected in Him: Come as we are with a willing heart. He will give us a new heart.
Randall doesn’t need to be perfect. He needs to do the very best he can.

scriptures.use: Read aloud together, then have three teams each make a poster for one phrase: come, deny yourselves, be perfected in Him.
Read after talking about the former missionary; ask what the Savior promises those who come to Him.
Read with the one-person challenge; ask how helping someone else could help with our own problems.
Optional: read after the sign comes down to see how much the Savior was willing to suffer for each of us.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
aligned_quotes.text: Jesus Christ did all of this because He loves all of the children of God.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Rasband
aligned_quotes.text: We fail only when we give up and stop trying

invitations.text: I invite you, please come unto Christ and embrace His promise
My humble invitation to us all: Will you find one person and invite him or her to come unto Christ by exercising faith to follow His teachings, or invite a friend to meet with the missionaries?

takeaways: I come to Christ as I am; He does the perfecting.
The Lord asks for my very best and a willing heart, not a flawless record.
When I help one person come unto Christ, He helps me with my own problems.
act: Do the thing you wrote on the outside of your paper: come to the Savior this week in that one way, even if you do not feel ready.
Invite your one person to something specific before next Sunday.
When you mess up this week, pray that same day instead of waiting until you feel better about yourself.
Tell one friend who is hard on himself or herself what Sister Child learned in her answer to prayer.
music: I'm Trying to Be like Jesus
adapt: At home or with one or two youth: skip the teams; each person takes one phrase from Moroni 10:32, writes a six-word summary and explains it.
Short on time (15 minutes): do the sign on the door, the six-word summaries without posters, Sister Child’s answer to prayer, and the one-person challenge.
Large class: make six teams, two per phrase, and let the paired teams compete for the clearest poster.

children.title: Jesus Says, “Come”
children.big_idea: Jesus loves everyone and invites all of us to come to Him; I do not have to be perfect, I just do my best and He helps me.
children.objective: Children will say that Jesus invites everyone to come to Him, and will show one way they can come to Jesus and one way they can invite a friend.
prepare: Draw a large hand held up to say stop on one sheet of paper and write Keep Out under it. Bring tape.
Bring plain paper and crayons for each child.
Bring a soft ball and a box or basket.
Set two chairs a little apart at the front of the room to make a gate. Tape the Keep Out sign to one chair.
If you can, bring a picture of the Savior.

segments.name: Welcome and song
steps: Greet each child by name. Invite a child to pray.
Sing the song I Feel My Savior's Love.
Show the picture of the Savior and say: Jesus loves every one of us, and today we will learn something He says to everyone. He says, “Come.”

segments.name: The sign on the gate
steps: Point to the two chairs and the sign. Ask the first question.

Tell the story simply: a long time ago, a missionary named Elder Dube saw a sign on the gate of the mission office. It told people to stay out. President Oaks, who is now our prophet, asked for the sign to be taken down, because we invite everyone to come unto Christ.
Choose a child to take the sign off the chair. Then let every child walk through the gate, one at a time. As each one comes through, the class says together: “Jesus says, Come.”
When all are seated, ask the second question.
questions: What does this sign tell people to do?
Who does Jesus invite to come to Him?

segments.name: Come is an action
steps: Tell the children that Elder Dube said come is an action. It means we move.
Have the children stand along one wall. Stand across the room holding the picture of the Savior.
Name ways we come to Jesus, one at a time: I pray. I go to church. I read the scriptures. I am kind. I say sorry. Each time, the children repeat the words and take two big steps toward the picture.
When they reach you, have them sit in a circle and say together: I can come to Jesus.
questions: What is one way you came to Jesus this week?

segments.name: I can do my best
steps: Put the box on the floor. Let each child toss the ball once from a few steps away. Cheer for every try. Most will miss.
Say: No one gets it in every time. That is all right. Now stand beside each child, walk with the child right up to the box, and let him or her drop the ball in.

Tell the story: Elder Dube visited a good man named Brother Child, who was trying very hard to change something that was hard for him. His wife prayed and prayed for him. Heavenly Father answered her. The answer was that he did not need to be perfect. He needed to do the very best he could. Jesus helped him, and he and his wife went to the temple to be sealed.
Have the children repeat after you, with a thumbs-up: I do my best. Jesus helps me.
questions: When we try and it is still hard, who can help us?

segments.name: Make a welcome sign
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Say: The old sign told people to stay out. Let us make a new sign for the gate.
Invite the children to draw a sign that welcomes everyone to come to Jesus. They might draw an open gate, a smiling face, a heart or the Savior with children.
Help them write the word Come at the top.
As they draw, walk around and ask each child to tell you about the sign.
Tape one or two finished signs to the chairs where the old sign was.

segments.name: I can invite a friend
steps: Tell the children that Elder Dube asked all of us to find one person and invite him or her to come unto Christ.
Practice in pairs. One child stands at the gate and says, “Will you come with me?” The other says yes, and they walk through the gate together. Then they trade places.
Suggest things they could invite a friend to do: come to Primary, sit with me, pray with our family, come to an activity.
Ask each child to think of one person to be kind to or to invite this week. They do not have to say the name aloud.
questions: How do you feel when someone invites you to come along?

segments.name: Testimony and closing
steps: Ask the review questions and let several children answer.
Bear a short testimony: Jesus loves you. You do not have to be perfect to come to Him. When you do your best, He helps you.
Send the welcome signs home and ask the children to show a grown-up and tell them what Jesus says. Tell them that next week you will ask whom they invited and how they came to Jesus.
If time allows, sing the song I'm Trying to Be like Jesus. Close with prayer.
questions: What does Jesus say to everyone?
Do we have to be perfect to come to Jesus?

key_quotes.text: He invites us to come unto Him.
He needs to do the very best he can.

scriptures.use: Show the children where this verse is. Have an older child read the first few words, up to the name of Christ, and ask everyone to listen for the word come.
Tell the children in your own words that Jesus wants us to come to Him so we can have joy; older children can read it aloud during the welcome-sign activity.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
aligned_quotes.text: Jesus Christ did all of this because He loves all of the children of God.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Fale
aligned_quotes.text: I am a child of God and He loves me.

invitations.text: My humble invitation to us all: Will you find one person and invite him or her to come unto Christ by exercising faith to follow His teachings, or invite a friend to meet with the missionaries?

takeaways: Jesus invites everyone to come to Him.
I do not have to be perfect. I do my best and Jesus helps me.
I can invite a friend to come to Jesus too.
act: Come to Jesus every day this week by praying in the morning and at night.
Put your welcome sign where your family can see it and tell them what Jesus says.
Invite one person to come with you: to Primary, to play, or to sit with you.
When something is hard, say a prayer and try again.
music: I'm Trying to Be like Jesus

adapt.younger: Ages 3–7: keep the stories to three or four sentences each and let the children walk through the gate twice. Repeat the two short lines often with actions: beckon with a hand for come, thumbs-up for I do my best. Skip the pair practice; instead you stand at the gate, invite each child by name to come, and walk through together. Have a helper write Come on each sign.
adapt.older: Ages 8–11: have a child read Moroni 10:32 aloud and find the three things Elder Dube noticed in it. Ask a harder question: Why might someone think he or she is not good enough to come to Jesus, and what would you tell that person? Let older children lead the stepping activity by naming the ways we come to Jesus, and write their own invitation on the back of the sign.
